questions.text: Some people prefer studying alone, while others prefer studying in a group. Which do you prefer and why? Give specific reasons and examples.
questions.sampleAnswer: Personally, I prefer studying alone, although I think group study has some advantages. The main reason is concentration. When I study by myself, I can choose a quiet place, work at my own speed and spend more time on the topics I find difficult. In a group, the conversation often moves away from the subject, and I end up chatting instead of learning. That said, groups are useful just before an exam, because explaining an idea to someone else is a great way to check whether you really understand it. For example, last semester I studied alone for most of the term, and then met two classmates the week before the final exam to test each other. That combination worked really well for me. So, in conclusion, I prefer studying alone most of the time, but I use group sessions strategically.

questions.text: Should university education be free for all students? Discuss the advantages and disadvantages, and give your opinion.
Describe the school you went to as a child. What did you like and dislike about it?
Describe a technological invention that has improved your life. Explain how it has made a difference.
Many jobs may be replaced by machines and artificial intelligence in the future. How should society prepare for this change?
questions.sampleAnswer: Automation is likely to transform many industries, so society should prepare in three main ways. First, education systems need to focus less on memorising facts and more on skills that machines find difficult, such as creativity, critical thinking and working with people. Second, governments and companies should invest in retraining programmes, so that workers whose jobs disappear can move into new roles instead of becoming unemployed. For example, a factory worker could be trained to maintain the robots that replaced the old production line. Third, we may need to rethink social support, perhaps by strengthening unemployment benefits during periods of transition. Of course, technology will also create jobs that we cannot imagine today. Overall, I believe the change is not something to fear, as long as we plan for it early and make sure the benefits are shared fairly.

Describe your perfect weekend. What would you do, and who would you spend it with?
Is it better to live in a big city or in the countryside? Explain your answer with examples.
Describe a place you visited that was very different from your home. What surprised you the most?
Some people say that travelling is the best form of education. Do you agree? Explain why or why not.
Would you rather have a job with a high salary or a job you really enjoy? Explain your choice.
questions.sampleAnswer: If I had to choose, I would rather have a job I really enjoy, as long as the salary covers my basic needs. The main reason is that we spend a huge part of our lives at work. If I hated my job, a high salary would not make up for feeling stressed and unmotivated every single day. On the other hand, when you enjoy your work, you are usually more productive, and over time that can actually lead to promotions and a better income. For example, my uncle left a well-paid banking job to become a teacher. He earns less now, but he is far happier and healthier. Of course, money matters, especially for people supporting a family, so I would not choose a job that cannot pay the bills. But between a high salary and genuine satisfaction, I would choose satisfaction.
